newsitem.title: UK: IBCA assigns ratings to Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya.
newsitem.headline: IBCA assigns ratings to Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya.

text.p: IBCA said on Monday it assigned Thailand's Bank of Ayudhya an individual rating of C, and a legal rating of 2.
IBCA said in a statement that the bank is Thailand's fifth largest commercial bank and has an eight percent share of bank advances and nine percent of bank deposits.
The agency said it assigned the individual rating "on the premise that the bank is entirely independent and therefore unable to rely on the support of state authorities or its owners."
The Ratanarak family, with a holding understood to aproximate 35 percent, is the bank's largest shareholder, according to IBCA.
"As with all Thai banks, Bank of Ayudhya has benfited from a strongly growing Thai economy, which has posted growth rates of about 10.0 percent for the past decade," IBCA said.

Relative to the banking indsutry, the bank's loan portfolio is overweight in manufacturing and real estate, both of which are coming under pressure. Manufacturers are unable to compete with low labour costs in Indochina, and there is also substantial oversupply in the property sector.
However, Bank of Ayudhya profit performance has been solid and its loan loss reserves are maintained at a level well above the statutory minimum.
IBCA said unless the economic slowdown is sustained and impacts on a wide range of the bank's borrowers over a prolonged period, the bank should be well-placed to absorb potential losses.
"IBCA's ratings reflect the prospective deterioration in Thailand's economic environment which can be expected to some degree to negatively impact Bank of Ayudhya's balance sheet," the agency said.
"The bank would warrant a slightly higher rating were it not for the uncertainty created by Thailand's economic slowdown," it said.
